sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Tiger Census Methodology**: Uses the **M-STrIPES** (Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status) platform. It employs a double-sampling approach: camera trapping combined with occupancy modeling.
• **Lion Census Methodology**: Historically based on the **'Block Count' method** (direct sighting). Recent shifts include the **'Population Estimation Method'** (scientific sampling) to improve accuracy.
• **Institutional Oversight**: Tiger census is mandated by the **NTCA** (National Tiger Conservation Authority) under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. Lion census is primarily managed by the **Gujarat State Forest Department**.
• **Key Metric**: **Carrying Capacity** of the habitat is the limiting factor for population growth, determined by prey density and habitat connectivity.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Tiger Corridors**: Identification of 'Source-Sink' dynamics to maintain genetic flow.
• **Lion Translocation**: Supreme Court mandate to establish a second home for Asiatic lions (Kuno National Park) to prevent extinction from a single-point disaster.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Human-Wildlife Conflict (HWC), habitat fragmentation, and genetic bottlenecking in lions.
• **Solutions**: Landscape-level management, community-based conservation, and AI-driven monitoring.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'T-4-C' (Tiger-4-Camera) and 'L-5-G' (Lion-5-Gir).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Tiger census happens every 4 years using Camera traps; Lion census happens every 5 years in Gir.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Lion Census' as a national-level project similar to 'Project Tiger'. Remember, the Lion project is state-led with central assistance, whereas Project Tiger is a national statutory mandate.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Umbrella Species' for Tigers and 'Flagship Species' for Lions to demonstrate conceptual depth in biodiversity answers.

keyTakeaways: Tiger census is a national, scientific, 4-year cycle exercise under NTCA.
Lion census is a regional, 5-year cycle exercise focused on the Gir ecosystem.
Scientific methodology (Camera traps vs. Direct count) is the primary differentiator in data reliability.
